Hi Rafael,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call yesterday. Aurum's security team needs a short follow-up so our Legal/Compliance can accept Redwood's standard DPA language. Can you provide proposed clause text we can attach to the DPA, plus a checklist of the artifacts (audit logs, KV cache snapshots, request traces, raw prompt/response archival windows)? We're prioritizing turnaround this week; procurement needs the DPA redline by Friday to meet our quarter-close.

Laura —

Appreciate the clear asks. Drafted a short candidate clause and attached our internal "Retention Hold Playbook" which maps artifacts to retention windows and custody. Key notes up front:
- Redwood can enact a contractual retention hold that prevents automated erasure for specified datasets and timeboxes.
- Evidence we can provide: request/response logs (30 days live, 365 days archived on S3), system audit trail (7 years), per-request KV cache snapshots (redacted, 90 days), session-level tracing (90 days).
- For onshore/EU storage: primary logs live in the region of the tenant (we can arrange onshore archival for specific artifacts; see playbook appendix).

I've included a short clause below you can drop into the DPA. If you like it, Marissa and Neha are cc'ed to fast-track legal wording.

---DRAFT CLAUSE START---
Retention Hold. Upon written notice from Customer of a bona fide security incident or lawful request requiring preservation (a "Retention Hold"), Redwood will suspend automated deletion and export the preserved artifacts listed in the Evidence Checklist. The Preservation period will commence on Redwood's acknowledgment of the notice and will continue for the time reasonably necessary to complete Customer's investigation, not to exceed 180 days unless mutually agreed in writing. Redwood shall (a) maintain a read-only preserved copy of the specified artifacts, (b) provide secure access to Customer-specified investigators where reasonably practicable, and (c) retain an immutable audit trail of all access and export activity associated with the preserved artifacts.
---DRAFT CLAUSE END---

Next steps: if Aurum needs onshore archival of specific artifacts beyond our default archival, we can provide a scoped onshore-archival addendum (pricing/lead time will vary). DocuSign draft available if you want to mark this for procurement review.

Rafael
Director, Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Retention hold request for incident INV-2028-0419 - questions

Thanks Rafael — good start. A couple of redlines and clarifications from Legal/Compliance:

1) Timebox language: change "not to exceed 180 days unless mutually agreed" to "180 days, renewable upon written request with justification." Customers typically want the right to extend; procurement prefers a renewal path rather than open-ended mutual agreement language.

2) Evidence scope: need explicit list of artifacts Redwood will deliver on request. Suggest we enumerate as: 
   - Request/response logs (UTC timestamps, request id, model version) — archival retention: 365 days
   - System audit trail (admin actions, role changes, key rotations) — retention: 7 years
   - KV cache snapshots (redacted personally identifiable data) — retention: 90 days, exported as CSV on request
   - Binary model artifacts: not disclosed under retention hold unless court order

3) Onshore: include a sentence: "If Customer requires onshore retention of preserved artifacts, Redwood will provide a commercially reasonable proposal (including cost and timeline) within five (5) business days of receiving the request."

4) Access & export: require an attestation that Redwood will provide proof of integrity (checksums and audit logs) for any exported artifact.

I'll attach a proposed redline for the clause. Rafael — can you confirm whether request/response logs include the original prompt text by default? That is often a sticking point; we should also confirm redaction options.

Neha Kapoor
Sr. Counsel, Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Rafael/Neha/Team —

Thank you for the quick turnaround and the clear redlines. Aurum is comfortable with the revised timebox language and the onshore proposal timeline. Two quick follow-ups before we loop procurement: 

1) Prompt text: we do need request/response logs to contain original prompt text by default for investigative completeness. We understand customers can opt for prompt redaction; please document the redaction options and the operational impact (e.g., inability to recreate an interaction).

2) Evidence integrity: the checksum + audit trail approach is acceptable. Can Redwood confirm you can produce an immutable, signed checksum and access log for any exported snapshot? We will include that in an annex.

If those two items are confirmed, we can accept the clause as redlined and move to procurement/DocuSign. Please send the final redline and I'll route it internally.
